question: Will Hormuz reopen this year, yes or no?

lines.text: Trump has rejected Iran's seven-day plan to end the war, the Wall Street Journal reports.
lines.note: WSJ via Al Jazeera, Kurdistan24, 26 Sep

lines.text: Here's what Iran offered. In the first five days, the US lifts its naval blockade, eases oil sanctions and frees twelve billion dollars.
lines.note: Araghchi's plan, per Al Jazeera / Kurdistan24

lines.text: Day six, Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz. Day seven, nuclear talks begin.
Before the war, about 125 ships crossed Hormuz every day.
On Thursday, tracking data counted just nine.
Normally, about a fifth of the world's oil and gas goes through it.

scene.label: of the world's oil and LNG

lines.text: Iran's foreign minister says the choice is now America's.

scene.quote: The choice now rests with the United States.

lines.text: The White House hasn't formally announced a decision. US officials call the talks positive and constructive.
So, will Hormuz reopen this year? Yes or no?
